cards.title: StudyFetch Calendar 2.0 - the calendar decides what to study
cards.move: Open on the pain, not the product: the first beat is the student deciding what to study tonight, and the calendar answers it - exam, topics, mastery - so the UI enters as the answer to a question the viewer already has.
cards.why: StudyAI's hook is the same pain (page in, no idea where to start). Borrowing the problem-first order means the device beat proves something instead of introducing a screen.

cards.title: Gemini study notebooks - curiosity to comprehension
cards.move: Sell the transformation in one line and make free/available part of the promise, not a footnote: the film never lists features, it names the before and after state and closes on the access condition (free, every language).
cards.why: Our CTA already ends on 'جاهز أن تبدأ؟ مجانًا'; this is the register to keep - one transformation, then access, nothing invented about scale or ratings.

cards.title: Shape morphing through UI states - prompt-motion
cards.move: One element, never cut: size, radius and colour morph while the content swaps with a short blur, every value a closed-form spring summed per event, all of it a pure function of seek(t); drags are direct manipulation and the loop closes on frame 0.
cards.why: This is exactly how a UI beat should behave in our engine: no transitions, no state, one spring per change, so --concurrency=75% cannot change the picture.

cards.title: One-take flood handoff (photo print)
cards.move: the camera flies through a printed photo and the print becomes the next scene, so the cut happens inside one continuous move
cards.why: The store film must never cut; the storefront grows out of a Telegram bubble and the phone becomes the room — same flood grammar, no seam.

cards.title: Beat-locked 120 BPM UGC with event per bar
cards.move: one visual event per bar, hand-held micro-shake and a 3D hero camera instead of a new transition per scene
cards.why: Gives the 20-bar store film its rhythm: the same phone held by one continuous camera, with a new state in the UI on every bar.

cards.title: HadiType showreel — whole-word Arabic kinetic type
cards.move: Arabic words land as whole shaped units with weight flex and mask, not letter-by-letter
cards.why: The hook and CTA headlines are Arabic: shaping must never break, so the motion is word-level masks while the weight visibly flexes.

cards.title: Sahi — scale reveal / macro-to-context
cards.move: macro detail snaps back to full context in one move, proving scale instead of stating it
cards.why: The paid order and the admin dashboard are shown macro-first, then pulled back to the phone so the audience knows it is all in one hand.

cards.title: ElevenLabs Brand Kit — campaigns stay on-brand
cards.move: show the same asset across applications (type, colour, card, environment) as one system rather than a settings list, with every application snapping into place on the beat
cards.why: Gives the store-design beat a way to show swatches, type and cards as one coherent identity instead of a generic settings screen.

cards.title: zero — Opus 5.5 UI motion showreel prompt
cards.move: One element never cuts: it morphs size, radius and colour while its content swaps with a short blur; a cursor drives every change; the last frame equals the first.
cards.why: The sourcing and setup scenes are built on the same rule: one ledger line and one glass card family carry the eye, while the data changes on the bar instead of hard-cutting every card.
